Toggle button

A button that turns one view option on or off, such as Wrap lines, and says which with aria-pressed.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For an option of the current view that takes effect at once and is not saved as a setting: Wrap lines, Show whitespace, Show tool calls.
  • In a toolbar above a log, a diff or a transcript, in its small size.

When not to use it

  • For a setting that is stored, in a settings form. Use a switch, or a checkbox when it is sent with the form.
  • To choose one of several views, such as Unified or Split. Use a segmented control.
  • For an option with only an icon. Use an icon button with aria-pressed.
  • For an action that happens once, such as Copy. Use a button.

Variants

off
aria-pressed="false". Drawn as a plain button.
on
aria-pressed="true". A stronger border, a sunken fill and a bar under the label.

Sizes

default
44px tall.
small gw-button--small
The button component's small size: drawn 32px tall for a toolbar, with a 44px pointer target. Lay small toggles out with gw-cluster gw-gap-md, so the targets of two wrapped rows do not overlap.

Accessibility

  • Use a button element with type="button", the classes gw-button and gw-toggle-button, and aria-pressed set to "true" or "false". The attribute is always present, so a screen reader announces a toggle button in both states.
  • The label names the option and stays the same in both states: Wrap lines, never Unwrap lines. Only aria-pressed changes. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
  • The app flips aria-pressed on each press and applies the option at once. Nothing else is needed: the styles read aria-pressed only.
  • Never add gw-button--primary to show that an option is on.
  • Group related toggles in an element with role="group" and an aria-label that says what they change, such as Diff view options.
  • Tab reaches each toggle, and Enter and Space flip it. Both come from the button element.
  • Set the disabled attribute while the option cannot change. The bar stays, so the reader can still see which options were on.
  • A toggle button is never busy: the bar is drawn where the button component draws its spinner.
